The private banking arm of the US group surveyed 125 of what it called international family offices to discover what’s uppermost in their minds. International family offices are adding to equities and
  alternatives despite mounting geopolitical concern, with
  artificial intelligence now their dominant investment theme,
  according to JP Morgan Private Bank's International Family
  Office Pulse Survey. Of the 125 family offices polled, 74 per cent (92 respondents)
  named AI as a top investment priority. Some 66 per cent cited
  geopolitical risk as their single greatest portfolio concern,
  ahead of asset valuations at 54 per cent and persistent inflation
  at 43 per cent, JP
  Morgan said. The family offices polled were from Europe,
  Middle East and Africa, Latin America, and Asia-Pacific. Public equities were the most common destination for new capital
  over the past six months, with 25 per cent of respondents (31
  family offices) increasing allocations. Of those, 81 per cent
  also named AI as a priority theme. The bank said this shows that
  the move into equities is closely tied to conviction on AI. “Many feel strongly that the risk of staying out is higher than
  the risk of getting in,” Natacha Minniti, global co-head of the
  family office practice at JP Morgan Private Bank, said. Alternatives are also attracting fresh money. Some 43 per cent of
  respondents made new allocations to the asset class in the past
  six months. The bank described this as a strategic shift rather
  than routine rebalancing, driven by persistent inflation and a
  need for income. The US banking group said its findings also drew on The 2026
  Family Office Report, a global study with a broader 2025
  respondent base spanning all geographies. Nervousness

  fastest-rising themes in the survey. William Sinclair, global co-head of the family office practice

  “This is structural, not cyclical. The global order is
  fragmenting, raising the cost of stability and permanently
  reshaping the opportunity set.” After AI, infrastructure ranks as the most popular theme and is a

  follows at 26 per cent, covering biotech, medtech, AI-driven

title: JPMorgan Tops AI Rankings Again: Can Its Spending Boost Returns? - The Globe and Mail
content: JPMorgan JPM has retained the top spot in the 2026 Evident AI Index for Banks for the fifth consecutive year, underscoring its leadership as artificial intelligence (AI) adoption accelerates across the banking industry. The bank ranked first or second across all four of Evident’s assessment pillars — talent, innovation, leadership and transparency.However, for investors, the key question is whether JPMorgan’s substantial technology spending can generate commensurate financial and productivity benefits. The banking giant has earmarked roughly $19.8 billion for technology in 2026, including continued investments in AI, data and infrastructure. Management believes these investments are already producing measurable value across credit, fraud detection and personalization.AI adoption is also becoming increasingly embedded in JPMorgan’s operations. During the 2026 Company Update in February, CEO Jamie Dimon said its internal LLM Suite is used by roughly 150,000 employees weekly, with users estimating around four hours of weekly time savings. More than 90% of Commercial & Investment Bank engineers use AI coding assistants, while AI-driven transaction screening has more than doubled processing volumes and halved manual checks.JPMorgan has also doubled its AI use cases in production and identified roughly $600 million in efficiencies, some AI-related. Yet, converting productivity gains into directly measurable earnings remains challenging. For investors, AI could strengthen JPMorgan’s long-term operating leverage and competitive positioning, though elevated investment requirements and uncertain monetization keep the near-term risk-reward equation balanced. Two close peers of JPMorgan are Bank of AmericaBAC and Citigroup C.Bank of America is scaling AI across customer service, software development and employee workflows. EricaAssist shortens call times, while AI coding tools have lifted developer productivity by more than 20%. AI also automates research, document processing and client-meeting preparation, reducing manual work and supporting lower operating costs and improved efficiency at Bank of America.Citigroup is expanding AI across coding, client service, onboarding and risk workflows. More than 10,000 engineers use advanced AI tools, creating roughly 100,000 hours of weekly capacity. title: J.P. Morgan lifts 2026-end target for S&P 500 to 8,000 on AI, earnings strength - The Standard (HK)
content: J.P. Morgan raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 index to 8,000 from 7,800 on Monday, citing prospects of solid corporate earnings and rising confidence that AI investments by large hyperscalers would drive faster revenue growth. The new target implies about 3.1 percent upside from the index's last close of 7,757.64 and adds to a growing wave of bullish calls, with at least seven brokerages now expecting the benchmark to reach the 8,000 level by 2026-end. Morgan analysts said. The brokerage also revised its S&P 500 earnings-per-share forecasts to US$365 (HK$2,847) for 2026 and to US$420 for 2027. J.P. Morgan said the benefits of rising AI investments were clearer in the second quarter, especially at Google, Amazon and Microsoft, as strong cloud growth, larger backlogs and better cash-flow visibility eased investor concerns about returns on spending. Despite the strong earnings backdrop, J.P. Morgan maintained its forward valuation multiple target at about 20 times, citing higher interest rates, geopolitical risks and a large supply of equity and debt issuance. The S&P 500 has gained 13.3 percent so far this year, buoyed by AI optimism, even as uncertainty over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and talks involving Iran, Oman and the United States has kept pressure on oil markets and shipping.

The prior report was striking. The bank posted a record quarterly result, helped by exceptional equity trading, a rebound in dealmaking advisory fees and growth in asset and wealth management. That showing surprised many observers and reinforced the view that the franchise is firing on nearly every cylinder. Shares have traded steadily in the run-up to the report, reflecting a market that appreciates the bank's consistency without expecting dramatic surprises. Broader financial stocks have also been firm today, supported by a constructive tone across equities and a rally in technology and semiconductor names. The central appeal of JPMorgan lies in the breadth of its business. Rather than relying on a single line, the bank earns money from consumer deposits and loans, credit cards, commercial lending, corporate advisory work, securities trading, payments processing and wealth management. When one area slows, another often accelerates. This diversity has been on full display recently. Trading desks benefited from volatile and active markets, while advisory teams saw a revival in mergers, acquisitions and capital markets issuance. At the same time, steady growth in deposits and credit card balances supported the consumer side of the house. One of the most important questions for any large bank is the health of the consumer. So far, American households have remained resilient, with employment broadly stable, wages growing and spending on travel, dining and retail staying firm. These conditions have kept delinquencies on credit cards and auto loans at manageable levels. The bank's consumer arm, which serves millions of households through branches, mobile apps and card products, offers a close view of spending patterns. Its commentary on payment volumes and balance growth is frequently cited as a real-time indicator of the broader economy, and it has generally pointed to continued strength. Markets have been active throughout the year, creating a favorable environment for trading businesses. Large swings in rates, currencies, commodities and equities have driven client activity, and JPMorgan's scale allows it to serve institutional customers across nearly every asset class and region. Gold trading near record highs and firmer crude prices have added to commodity flows, while a strong semiconductor rally has energized equity markets. Such conditions typically generate higher volumes, wider participation and greater demand for hedging products, all of which feed into trading revenue. Dealmaking advisory has staged a notable recovery. After a long period of subdued dealmaking, companies have returned to the market with acquisitions, public offerings and debt financings, encouraged by improved sentiment, easier financing conditions and a desire to reposition for new technologies such as artificial intelligence. JPMorgan has historically held a leading position in global advisory and underwriting, and the rebound has lifted fees significantly. Large transactions tied to data-center construction, power infrastructure and technology consolidation have been particularly active themes. Large banks sit at the heart of the economy, channeling savings into loans and providing the plumbing for payments and markets. JPMorgan's size gives it a prominent position in major benchmarks such as the S&P 500, and its performance often influences how the entire financial group is perceived. Within Bluechip Stocks, the bank is frequently viewed as a model of scale and resilience in financial services. Its ability to deliver steady results across different parts of the economic cycle has earned it a reputation as a bellwether for the health of the banking system. Net interest earnings remain the backbone of the banking model. The spread between what banks earn on loans and securities and what they pay on deposits has been supported by a stable rate environment, and the bank has guided that the trend should remain healthy even as benchmark rates drift lower. Deposit competition has eased compared with the period of intense pressure seen after regional bank failures. Customers have grown more comfortable with large institutions, and JPMorgan has benefited from its reputation as a safe haven, attracting stable balances across consumer and commercial accounts. Several challenges remain on the horizon. A sharper slowdown in the economy could raise credit losses, and a sudden shift in market conditions could dampen trading and advisory activity. Cyber threats and operational disruptions are also constant concerns for institutions of this size. Commercial real estate, particularly office properties, continues to face pressure in some markets, and while the bank's exposure is manageable, the issue remains a watched area for the sector. Consumer credit could also deteriorate if employment weakens, which would test the resilience of household balance sheets. ASML Holding NV (NASDAQ:ASML, XETRA:ASME), the Dutch semiconductor equipment maker, could deliver a stronger-than-expected 2027 outlook when it reports third-quarter results, JP Morgan analyst Sandeep Deshpande said. The bank expects ASML to signal robust demand, with initial indications for 2027 potentially exceeding current market consensus. ASML has outperformed its semiconductor equipment peers despite a weak sector backdrop, while its valuation has fallen to levels historically associated with semiconductor downturns. JP Morgan said there is currently little evidence of a downturn, and the semiconductor industry shows stable inventories and demand. The bank believes ASML has strong visibility into 2027, with most extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUV) orders for the year already committed and substantial demand also secured for deep ultraviolet (DUV) systems. ASML is likely to be booking orders for 2028 equipment, reinforcing the company’s visibility over future revenue, JP Morgan said. Bloomberg consensus currently expects ASML’s sales to rise by about 28% in the financial year 2027, while JP Morgan forecasts wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending of $224.5 billion, up 38% from the previous year. The bank said ASML could have scope to exceed current estimates if semiconductor equipment spending reaches its forecast, given the company has had significant lead time to prepare its manufacturing capacity. ASML has indicated it expects to ship about 85 EUV systems and 169 DUV immersion systems in 2027, with both targets potentially offering upside if suppliers can meet demand. JP Morgan therefore expects ASML to deliver a positive message on both demand and its ability to supply customers when it reports third-quarter results. The bank said continued earnings beats could support the shares because their current valuation appears to price in a semiconductor downturn that has yet to emerge. title: JPM Stock Gains Nearly 3% — Jamie Dimon Succession Dynamics Shift After Marianne Lake Exit - Stocktwits
content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. moved Troy Rohrbaugh and Doug Petno into co-president roles on Thursday, reshaping its top leadership ranks after the sudden exit of consumer banking head Marianne Lake. The changes add fresh momentum to the succession discussion around Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon. Shares of JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM) climbed nearly 3% on Thursday morning. JPMorgan said the elevation of Troy Rohrbaugh and Doug Petno to co-presidents effectively places them in senior leadership positions, strengthening the internal bench as part of its ongoing succession planning process. The new roles place Rohrbaugh and Petno as leading internal contenders in the long-term succession lineup for Dimon. Dimon described the changes as part of a broader leadership pipeline strategy, saying the bank is focused on strengthening its future executive ranks. He added that JPMorgan has “an exceptional group of senior leaders” across its operating committee and wider organization, expressing confidence in the company’s outlook. The leadership reshuffle also included significant retention incentives tied to long-term vesting. Petno and Rohrbaugh will each receive one-time awards of $30 million, while Chief Operating Officer Jenn Piepszak and asset and wealth management head Mary Erdoes will each receive $20 million, according to a regulatory filing. The awards are structured to vest over three years, highlighting the bank’s effort to retain key executives as it manages a broader leadership transition. Thursday’s developments came a day after JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced a $50-billion share buyback program and raised its quarterly dividend under its updated capital return plan. The board also approved a 10% increase in the payout to $1.65 per share from $1.50, effective in the third quarter of 2026. The buyback program is set to begin on July 1. Marianne Lake, CEO of Consumer and Community Banking and a long-time internal contender in the succession discussion, is retiring after more than 25 years with the firm. She will remain for a transition period, working with Rohrbaugh and other senior leaders to ensure an orderly handover. Her departure further reshapes the bank’s internal succession landscape. Lake becomes the latest senior executive to step away from consideration for the CEO role, following earlier changes including Jenn Piepszak’s move to COO in 2025 after opting out of the succession race, according to Bloomberg, adding that for more than a decade, speculation around Jamie Dimon’s eventual successor has remained a defining theme on Wall Street. Fermi LLC (FRMI) shares rallied nearly 9% in the premarket session on Thursday after the company's co-founder and largest individual shareholder, Toby Neugebauer, said he expected a tenant deal announcement soon. In a letter to shareholders, Neugebauer said he had “a high degree of confidence” about the deal announcement, adding that, ”I can say that because our deal team was in the contracting phase before our departure.” Neugebauer said recent developments have strengthened his confidence that Fermi is close to announcing a tenant or joint venture agreement, pointing to TDK's completion of the Fermi 2.0 engineering and project management agreement and the company's own statement that it expects to announce one or more such transactions. “Assuming the Company's announcement is the group we teed up, the Neugebauer family likes that tenant a lot,” he said. He also added that the transition to the "Fermi 2.0" strategy was intended to meet the requirements of large customers. “I know the project financing market was ready as well—we built that trust with them most notably from our firm stance on tenant one,” Neugebauer said. Neugebauer's letter to shareholders comes amid a proxy campaign after he was removed from his position in April. Fermi then appointed an interim leadership team to search for a permanent CEO. In response, Neugebauer launched a proxy campaign to call a special meeting, advocating for board changes, stronger corporate governance, and a review of all strategic alternatives, including a potential sale of the company. Fermi pushed back, rejecting Neugebauer's proposal to sell the business and instead reaffirming its commitment to its "Fermi 2.0" strategy. Neugebauer called on shareholders to vote for a Special Meeting to decide on Board composition. Neugebauer argued that while a tenant announcement could boost Fermi's stock in the near term, it would only mark the beginning of the company's execution phase and should not preclude the board from evaluating other strategic alternatives. “The proxy was never about a tenant. It was about restoring normal governance to Fermi, ensuring all strategic alternatives are honestly evaluated, and giving every shareholder the best risk-adjusted outcome,” Neugebauer said in the letter. “A tenant deal and broken governance can both be true at the same time,” he added. QuantumScape stock is drawing attention and at the center of a growing debate after CNBC's “Mad Money” host Jim Cramer revisited the energy storage company’s dramatic rise and fall, even as new partnerships continue to strengthen its standing in the automotive industry. Speaking about its SPAC-era history, Cramer pointed to QuantumScape as a reminder of the speculative excesses that surrounded electric-vehicle-related stocks during the 2020 and 2021 market boom. Cramer said investors embraced lofty expectations long before the company had a commercial product or meaningful sales. “QuantumScape, which in retrospect was basically a science experiment looking to develop better battery technology for electric vehicles. Anyone can develop better, more efficient batteries with the ability to charge very quickly, and you can make a killing even in a world where electric cars have lost some of their luster. But QuantumScape was a long way from having anything they could actually commercialize and they could sell. Even four years later, these guys still didn't have any meaningful revenue,” said Cramer. During the height of investor enthusiasm for electric-vehicle-related companies in 2020 and early 2021, QuantumScape attracted attention after it entered public markets via a special purpose acquisition company, or SPAC. Following the merger announcement, the SPAC in question saw its share price soar, and QuantumScape eventually climbed to nearly $132 per share in late 2020. The stock became one of the standout beneficiaries of speculative trading tied to the broader EV boom. Cramer said sentiment shifted once investors began focusing more closely on profitability, revenue generation and commercialization timelines. He also pointed to criticism from short sellers, which added pressure as questions emerged about the company’s prospects. “Then we started seeing short sellers come out of the woodwork, arguing it was a scam, and Wall Street gradually lost interest in companies with zero profitability, let alone super speculative names like QuantumCape. No revenue. In the end, the stock got obliterated by late 2022 and was in the single digits and has only been able to bounce above those levels at times thanks to what I regard as an occasional short squeeze,” he added. title: JP Morgan and Brown Advisory US small cap trusts to merge - Portfolio Adviser
content: The JP Morgan US Smaller Companies Investment Trust (JUSC) and Brown Advisory US Smaller Companies (BASC) have agreed to merge. The deal would see BASC reconstructed and its shareholders offered the opportunity to roll their investment into an enlarged JUSC, or sell for cash. The enlarged trust would continue to be managed by JP Morgan Asset Management in line with  the existing investment objective and policy. The trusts said they would benefit from greater scale and liquidity, Lower costs, enhanced discount management and established teams an investment processes. The annual management fee for the combined vehicle would be cut to 0.65% on the first £200m of net assets and 0.60% thereafter. JUSC is managed by Don San Jose, alongside co-portfolio managers Dan Percella and Jon Brachle. Shareholder documentation is set to be published by mid-November 2026, with the transaction expected to complete in December 2026 or shortly after, subject to approvals. See also: SJP shuffles manager line-up and trims corporate bonds Dominic Neary, chair of JUSC, said: “I am delighted to announce a proposed combination with BASC and look forward to welcoming those shareholders who participate in the rollover option. “I believe that US smaller companies are some of the most exciting in the world, with JUSC’s investment trust structure providing a marked advantage in accessing these opportunities. “There are significant benefits of this combination for all shareholders. With increased scale ever more important in the investment trust market, shareholders in the combined JUSC will benefit from an enlarged vehicle, with improved liquidity and lower ongoing costs.” QuotedData senior analyst Matthew Read said: “When BASC launched its strategic review in July, we questioned whether it could satisfy shareholders wanting a substantial cash exit while retaining the scale needed to remain viable. “The board appears to have reached much the same conclusion. Its solution looks sensible: shareholders wanting out can receive cash at just a 0.75% discount to residual NAV, while those who still believe in the US smaller companies opportunity can roll into JUSC without triggering an immediate capital gains tax liability.” © Copyright 2026 Mark Allen Group. The enlarged trust would continue to be managed by JP Morgan Asset Management in line with JUSC’s existing investment objective and policy. According to concurrent stock exchange notices today (7 October), the proposed transaction would see BASC reconstructed and its shareholders offered either the opportunity to roll their investment into an enlarged JUSC or elect to realise some or all their holding for cash, at a discount of 0.75% to BASC's residual net asset value. The enlarged trust would continue to be managed by JP Morgan Asset Management in line with JUSC's existing investment objective and policy. JP Morgan and Aberdeen UK small cap trusts to merge The move follows a strategic review by the BASC board, announced in July, with the rollover proposals providing "an attractive solution for shareholders who wish to retain exposure to US smaller companies through a larger investment trust with lower ongoing costs". Among the benefits of the proposal, JUSC and JP Morgan have agreed a further reduction in the annual management fee for the combined vehicle to 0.65% on the first £200m of net assets, and 0.6% thereafter. That would mean annual cost savings of approximately 20 basis points for BASC shareholders who roll over and approximately 13 basis points for existing JUSC shareholders. Alongside continuing share buybacks and regular five-yearly continuation votes, JUSC has also committed to an additional five-yearly conditional tender offer from 1 January 2027 for 30% of JUSC's shares at a 2% discount to NAV. The tender would be triggered if both JUSC underperforms the Russell 2000 Index, in sterling terms with net dividends reinvested, over the preceding five years, and its average share price discount to NAV is wider than 5% over the preceding 12 months. Additionally, the BASC board has also negotiated an "irrevocable undertaking" from US activist Saba Capital Management to vote in favour of the scheme and elect for a cash exit from its 16% BASC holding, rather than roll in to JUSC. 'Chaotic politics' causing disconnect between economic pressure and strong equity earnings The merger is expected to occur in Q4 2026, subject to shareholder approval. BASC chair Stephen White said: "The proposed combination with JUSC provides the right balance of choice and long-term opportunity. "For shareholders who wish to remain invested, it preserves exposure to US smaller companies through an investment trust structure, while offering the benefits of a larger vehicle, improved liquidity and lower ongoing costs." JUSC chair Dominic Neary added the combinations increased scale provides a compelling platform for shareholders to "invest in the heart of America". The £244.6m JP Morgan trust is currently trading at an 8.8% discount, according to data from the Association of Investment Companies. It has significantly underperformed its benchmark, the Russell 2000 Index (£), over one, three and five years, with a cumulative share price total return of 8.8%, 19.1% and 5.3%, respectively, as of 31 August. That compares to the benchmark's cumulative return of 25.8%, 50.5% and 39.9% over the same periods. JPMAM's Simon Crinage joins board of Polar Capital Technology trust Although the combination was considered a good deal for BASC shareholders overall by Winterflood's head of investment companies research Emma Bird, she said it was "slightly surprising" to see JUSC selected as the rollover option given its underperformance. However, "we have sympathy with the reasons given for both funds' underperformance versus the benchmark in recent years, with the market having favoured a small number of stocks in themes such as AI and cryptocurrency", she continued, while JUSC was "the only option" to allow investors to remain invested in a US Smaller Companies strategy. QuotedData senior analyst Matthew Read added: "When BASC launched its strategic review in July, we questioned whether it could satisfy shareholders wanting a substantial cash exit while retaining the scale needed to remain viable. The board appears to have reached much the same conclusion. "This may not be the outcome BASC's board envisaged when the review began, but it looks like a pragmatic solution that gives shareholders a genuine choice while avoiding the risk of leaving behind a subscale trust." title: Bridging Generations: J.P. Morgan And The Future Of Asian Wealth - Forbes Asia Custom
content: As Asia’s entrepreneurs and investors become increasingly global, wealth advisory is expanding beyond investment advice to help families navigate succession, family governance and wealth preservation across the generations. For many families, the challenge is less about “finding the next opportunity” and more about aligning family members on purpose and values across borders and generations. For Harshika Patel, a career in wealth management was never part of the plan. Growing up in an immigrant family, she had little exposure to the world of private banking that she would eventually come to help shape. Patel trained as a chartered accountant before building a career in treasury and financial markets. She moved into wealth advisory three years ago and today leads one of Asia’s largest wealth management businesses at J.P. Morgan. “If you’d said to me when I was growing up that one day I would be in wealth management, I would have laughed. I didn’t even know what wealth was,” she says. Patel’s route into leadership was similarly unconventional. Not always the candidate who fit the traditional mold, she was recognized by senior leaders for her drive, resilience and ability to make an impact through her teams. That experience now informs how she recruits and develops talent. Qualifications and expertise matter, but Patel also looks for curiosity, character and the will to contribute. She advocates hiring laterally from outside the traditional industry pool, believing that different experiences can lead to better questions and closer relationships with clients. Over time, she has focused on building a deliberately diverse business—across backgrounds, disciplines and ways of thinking—so teams can connect through shared context and lived experience, not only technical knowledge. That breadth is particularly valuable in the wealth advisory business, where clients come from very different backgrounds and value different perspectives. On the one hand Patel may leverage her experience over three decades to connect with an entrepreneur who has built a company from modest beginnings, while her team can bring expertise across a broad range of other topics, from legacy planning, investing in passion assets to philanthropy. Building those connections requires colleagues to understand one another as people, too. Within J.P. Morgan’s multicultural Asia business, Patel encourages team members to share the experiences behind their professional titles, from raising families and balancing work to navigating their own leadership journeys. Finding common ground, she believes, builds trust and allows bankers to connect more authentically with the diverse client base. “When we look past our differences long enough to find common ground, trust grows. And when trust grows, collaboration accelerates,” she explains. Her leadership at J.P. Morgan was recognized recently when The Asset named her “Private Banker of the Year for Asia” at its 2026 Private Capital Leadership Awards. In honoring Patel, the publication highlighted her steady hand during a period of rapid change in how wealth advisory teams serve ultra-high net worth (UHNW) clients. The publication cited her hands-on approach during volatile markets and her work helping Asia’s wealthiest families preserve and transfer their legacies. In total, J.P. Morgan earned a record 10 accolades at the awards, including “Asia’s Best Private Bank,” and “Best Private Bank for Family Office, UHNWIs – Asia.”* Those accolades have come when wealth itself is changing across the region. Technology has created new fortunes, while traditional industries such as manufacturing, real estate and resources continue to generate wealth. At the same time, shifting supply chains are creating new opportunities throughout Southeast Asia and beyond. Capital markets have also expanded rapidly, producing a new generation of investors and financial professionals. “When you look at the world’s top 10 stock markets today, six are in Asia. And as these companies become more valuable, the families and entrepreneurs behind them become wealthier,” Patel says. Many of these business owners now operate across several markets globally, while their families and investments are also increasingly spread around the world. As such, managing their companies, portfolios and family interests through volatile and complex environments has become as important as creating wealth. As families globalize, complexity rises: tax, residency, education, governance and decision rights can all span jurisdictions. Geopolitical shifts add another layer of uncertainty. “Geopolitics and its impact on their core business is probably the thing that keeps them awake at night the most,” Patel says. Those concerns have prompted many clients to diversify both their businesses and their wealth geographically. Supporting them requires expertise that reaches beyond traditional investment advice. Rather than treating wealth management as a standalone service, J.P. Morgan draws on expertise across its investment bank, corporate bank and broader global franchise. Says Patel: “J.P. Morgan operates in 100 markets globally across every dimension that families and business owners would need.” An entrepreneur seeking advice on financing an overseas acquisition may also require support managing personal investments, establishing structures for the next generation or helping children studying abroad. Increasingly, families prefer these conversations to happen within one institution rather than across multiple advisors. J.P. Morgan also tailors its coverage to clients with distinct needs. Its Financial Leaders Group, for instance, is set up to serve the unique needs of hedge fund managers, private equity investors and other senior financial executives. As families expand across markets and generations, trust and stability become increasingly important. Patel says clients value not only J.P. Morgan’s global capabilities, but also the confidence that comes from the firm’s fortress balance sheet and long-term approach to supporting families. J.P. Morgan has been operating in the Asia-Pacific region for over 100 years and today is present across 17 markets in the region. More broadly, wealthy Asian families are adopting longer investment horizons. Increasingly, Patel notes, many are moving away from highly transactional portfolios toward diversified, institutional-style strategies intended to withstand different market conditions and support wealth across generations. That focus on preserving wealth naturally raises the question of who will manage it in the future. For many families, the answer begins with preparing the next generation. Succession discussions now encompass governance, leadership and the responsibilities that accompany an inheritance. Future family leaders may have very different ambitions. Some want to run the family business, while others pursue independent careers but remain involved in managing family assets or philanthropy. Many have studied and worked internationally and expect a more collaborative relationship with their advisors. “No two next-gen leaders are the same. Even within a family, you can have siblings with different priorities and objectives,” says Patel. J.P. Morgan engages its next-generation clients as a distinct segment, with their own specific set of needs. Its programs combine investment education, leadership development and family governance, with vital networking opportunities for participants to connect with their peers. One recent program brought together teenagers from client families for sessions on investing and executive presence, as well as visits to technology companies. The bank also brings together families facing similar issues and draws on specialists in family governance who have spent decades helping families navigate succession. As a new generation prepares to take the reins of Asia’s wealthiest families, Patel believes the opportunity lies in helping them navigate the increasingly complex responsibilities that accompany lasting wealth. title: JPMorgan Q3 earnings preview: Can strong banking momentum continue? - MarketPulse
content: Ahead of next Tuesday’s Q3 2026 earnings on 13 October, JPMorgan Chase (JPM) remains the key bellwether for U.S. banking risk appetite. It will release its financial report card at around 7:00 a.m. ET, followed by its earnings call at 8:30 a.m. ET. The stock’s reaction will likely hinge on whether the bank can show that Q2’s strong profitability, trading revenue and investment banking momentum were not peak-cycle conditions. Based on Google Finance estimates for JPM’s Q3 earnings results, the consensus is for earnings per share (EPS) of US$5.91 and revenue of US$51.15 billion. Options markets data as of 5 October are pricing roughly a ±4.4% earnings move, above JPM’s 10-year average peak earnings-day move of ±3.4%, so the market is expecting a bigger-than-normal reaction. The bar is high because Q2 was exceptionally strong, with JPM reporting US$21.2 billion in net income, US$7.70 in EPS, US$58.0 billion in managed revenue, 29% Return on Tangible Common Equity (ROTCE), and a 14.1% standardised Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio. Excluding significant items, EPS was US$6.14, and ROTCE was 23%. The first key focus is net interest income (NII). JPMorgan’s core banking engine remains supported by higher-for-longer interest rates, resilient deposit balances and stronger card/wholesale loan activity. NII was US$25.6 billion in Q2, up 10% year on year, while NII excluding Markets was US$23.7 billion, up 4% year on year. A stable or better-than-expected NII print would reinforce the bank’s earnings floor and support its premium valuation. However, any sign of margin pressure from rising deposit costs or weaker loan growth could weigh on the stock. The second major driver is investment banking fees. Q2 investment banking fees for JPM rose 30% year on year, with equity underwriting up 78%, advisory fees up 20%, and debt underwriting fees up 19%. Traders will watch whether M&A advisory, IPO activity, and debt/equity underwriting continue to recover after a strong Q2, during which Reuters reported that Q2 was boosted by IPO activity, including SpaceX’s trillion-dollar listing, and major dealmaking such as the NextEra-Dominion transaction. A firm deal pipeline would signal that corporate confidence is improving and that the Wall Street fee cycle is reopening. Softer backlog commentary, however, would raise the risk that Q2 was a one-off spike rather than the start of a sustained capital-markets recovery. Global Markets’ revenue will be another important swing factor. Q2 Markets revenue was US$12.1 billion, up 35% year on year, driven by Equity Markets revenue up 86% and Fixed Income Markets revenue up 6%. Elevated cross-asset volatility, shifting Fed expectations and active equity markets should support client activity across Fixed Income, Currencies, and Commodities (FICC) and equities trading. A strong Global Markets print would help offset any softness in traditional banking or advisory revenue. But if trading momentum slows sharply, the market may start to question whether JPM’s recent earnings strength is losing pace. Credit quality is the main downside risk; Q2 credit costs were US$2.5 billion, including US$2.4 billion of net charge-offs and a US$149 million reserve build. Investors will focus on card charge-offs, reserve builds, commercial real estate exposure and broader consumer resilience. Stable credit costs would support the soft-landing narrative for banks. A larger reserve build or rising consumer delinquencies would be negative, as it would shift attention from earnings upside to late-cycle credit deterioration. Expense discipline also matters. Q2 expense was US$27.3 billion, up 15% year on year, driven by compensation, front-office headcount, brokerage/distribution fees, marketing, technology and occupancy costs. JPMorgan can absorb higher compensation, technology and front-office costs if revenue momentum remains strong. But if expenses rise while trading or investment banking revenue slows, operating leverage will deteriorate, capping upside for the stock. The market is moving into Q3 earnings season with stronger-than-usual earnings momentum. Based on a FactSet Insight report dated 5 October 2026, a record-high 72 S&P 500 companies have issued positive Q3 EPS guidance, exceeding the 5-year average of 42 and the 10-year average of 40. JPM also reports at a time when rate expectations, rising sovereign bond yields, AI-linked equity volatility and consumer resilience are all in focus. Reuters noted investors are becoming more cautious about whether the U.S. profit boom can continue, even though 2026 earnings growth remains strong. Hence, higher-for-longer rates can boost the bank’s NII but also increase credit risk and pressure valuations. For JPM, the best macro mix is firm loan growth, stable deposits, resilient consumers, active deal markets and no sharp deterioration in credit. Overall, the bull case for JPMorgan is a clean earnings beat driven by resilient NII, strong Global Markets revenue, improving investment banking fees, stable credit costs and continued capital returns. The bear case is not necessarily a bad quarter, but rather a “good but slowing” quarter in which Q2’s record momentum fades. JPMorgan is still the benchmark U.S. bank, but next Tuesday’s results need to prove that profitability, capital-markets activity and credit quality remain strong enough to justify its premium valuation. Let’s now decipher the multi-week outlook of JPM from a technical analysis lens. The major uptrend phase of JPM remains intact, as current price action has traded above the major ascending channel support in place since the 7 April 2025 low of 202.16 and the key 200-day moving average. The recent corrective decline of 11% (high to low) from the current all-time high of 366.50 printed on 13 August 2026 to the 1 October 2026 low of 325.87 has managed to stall right above the major ascending channel support and 200-day moving average, as well as retraced 61.8% of its prior medium-term bullish impulsive up move sequence from the 20 May 2026 low to the 13 August 2026 all-time high. The daily RSI momentum indicator has reached 31.62 on 30 September 2026, close to its oversold zone (below the 30 level) and to the level of 31.47 printed on 12 March 2026, which triggered a prior medium-term bullish reversal in JPM. These observations suggest a potential fresh multi-term bullish reversal scenario for JPM if the 323.00/315.70 key medium-term pivotal support holds. A clearance above the 351.55 potential upside trigger level (also the 50-day moving average acting as a resistance) may see a retest on the current all-time high of 366.50 in the first step before the next medium-term resistances come in at 379.66/381.53 and 394.68 (Fibonacci extension clusters and upper boundary of the major ascending channel). On the other hand, a break and a daily close below 315.70 would invalidate the recovery scenario, exposing the next medium-term supports at 293.94 and 280.00. A premium may be justified by durable profitability, but only if it compensates investors for cyclical credit and funding risks. title: J.P. Morgan’s Retirement Link Adds Lifetime Income Access - 401k Specialist
content:
Updates to the platform also include multilingual participant communications and education, plus easier RMD processing J.P Morgan Asset Management is boosting the capabilities of its Retirement Link offering to allow better access to in-plan retirement income products, among other updates designed to improve the experience of plan participants. In an announcement Tuesday, the company said Retirement Link, an offering focused on 401(k), 403(b) and nonqualified plans, will include broader access to J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s SmartRetirement Lifetime Income, which uses a target-date format to establish a stream of income in retirement. Other enhancements include better implementation and ongoing plan sponsor operations, and much improved participant education and plan communications, including more multilingual options. “We believe these expanded capabilities can strengthen retirement readiness by delivering clearer education and access to our retirement income solutions.” “Helping participants achieve a secure retirement is at the core of everything we do,” said Steve Rubino, Head of Retirement at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, in a release. “We believe these expanded capabilities can strengthen retirement readiness by delivering clearer education and access to our retirement income solutions.” These latest developments of Retirement Link’s capabilities are being delivered through an expanded connection with Empower, its recordkeeper of choice since 2012. Joe Smolen, President of Empower Workplace Solutions, said he is happy to help meet the evolving needs of retirement plan participants. “Our longstanding relationship with J.P Morgan Asset Management has been built on a shared commitment to helping individuals achieve their financial goals,” Smolen said. The revised focus on retirement income reflects the findings of J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s 2026 Defined Contribution Plan Participant Survey, which found that a vast majority of participants wished to make their retirement and investment planning as easy and thorough as possible. The survey indicated that 91% of participants showed interest in having in-plan guaranteed retirement income solutions. An additional 75% said they’d likely keep their assets in-plan if their existing plan offered an income solution. Other updates include changes to help bolster the implementation and onboarding experience for participants to make it an easier process, through the use of additional resources and technology. Plan sponsors will have better operational services, such as enhanced RMD processing to help simplify and reduce daily administrative work. Critical to participant success, the new Retirement Link upgrades will add a range of engagement resources and educational support, including multilingual resources. These will all help provide participants with better understanding about how their contributions are connected to investments, oversight and ultimately better retirement preparedness. The Retirement Link and Everyday 401(k) are two components of J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s retirement recordkeeping platform, geared at both new plan sponsors and established small- to mid-market plans. • Gen X, Millennial Savers Lack Confidence in Retirement System• Lifetime Income Can Help Ease Retirees’ Spending Fears• Participants Want Simpler 401(k) Decisions: JPMAM Survey News, insights, and analysis on the trends, products, and policy shaping the retirement plan industry.  goes ex-dividend today, Tuesday, even as the largest American bank by assets prepares to open the quarterly reporting season for the big lenders in about a week. The timing places the stock at an unusual intersection, where a routine cash distribution meets heightened curiosity about trading desks, lending demand and the cost of funding in a market where Treasury yields have pushed higher. Shares have been trading modestly below their record peak in recent sessions, with price moves staying contained compared with the sharper swings seen at some rivals. Several Wall Street brokerages have trimmed their published price expectations ahead of the report, yet the stock has remained anchored near the middle of its recent range, a sign that sentiment around the name is cautious rather than fearful. JPMorgan Chase operates one of the most diversified franchises in global finance. Its consumer and community banking arm serves millions of households through branches, digital channels and a large credit card business. A separate corporate and advisory banking division advises companies, underwrites securities and runs major markets desks. Alongside those segments sit commercial banking, which serves midsize firms, real estate developers and public-sector clients, and asset and wealth management, which looks after portfolios for institutions and affluent families. This blend means revenue arrives from net interest earnings, fees, trading activity and advisory mandates, rather than from a single source. Higher Treasury yields shape the earnings picture for any large lender. Banks typically earn the spread between what they charge on loans and securities and what they pay on deposits and other funding. When yields climb, the assets on a balance sheet can reprice upward, although deposit costs may also rise as customers seek better rates elsewhere. JPMorgan Chase has long been viewed as a bank with a large and sticky deposit base, which can soften the effect of competition for funding. The firm also carries a substantial securities portfolio whose value moves inversely with yields, so a rise in rates can influence both reported earnings and the accounting treatment of unrealized gains and losses. One of the more constructive themes in the industry has been the firm pace of capital-markets work. Corporate debt issuance has stayed active, equity underwriting has shown signs of recovery, and advisory pipelines have been described by bankers as healthier than in recent years. The consumer business is the other pillar of the story. American households have continued to spend, supported by a resilient labor market, and card balances have kept growing. JPMorgan Chase is among the largest card issuers in the country, so spending patterns feed directly into its quarterly numbers. Financial Stocks have been in focus this week as the large banks line up to report. The group has been influenced by shifting expectations about central bank moves, the slope of the yield curve and the regulatory environment, all of which feed into how lenders are viewed by the wider market. Regulatory developments have also been in the background. Discussions about capital requirements and stress-testing rules have kept the sector alert, since changes to required buffers can affect how much capital a bank can return to stockholders or deploy into lending and trading balance sheets. The cash dividend that goes ex-dividend today is part of a broader capital framework. JPMorgan Chase maintains capital ratios comfortably above regulatory minimums, which gives the board room to maintain distributions while still supporting lending growth and strategic spending. JPMorgan Chase spends heavily on technology, and the bank has spoken frequently about using artificial intelligence across software development, fraud detection, client service and internal research. These efforts aim to raise efficiency and to improve the experience for both retail and corporate customers. Competition remains intense. Rival megabanks such as Bank of America, Citigroup and Wells Fargo contest the same customers in consumer, card and commercial lending, while Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley compete fiercely in advisory, underwriting and wealth management. The wider equity market has been navigating a mix of firm economic data, elevated yields and debate over how quickly the central bank will ease. Financial shares have often moved in step with changes in the yield curve, rising when a steeper curve improves lending spreads and slipping when growth worries intensify. Broader benchmarks such as the S&P 500 have continued to hover near elevated levels, which helps sustain wealth-management fees tied to asset values and supports the willingness of companies to come to market. When the bank releases its quarterly results, attention is likely to center on net interest earnings guidance, loan and deposit growth, advisory and underwriting fees, trading revenue and reserve movements. title: Corteva Soars 11% on JPM Upgrade: “Undervalued at Current Price” - TIKR.com
content: Robert Kneschke and yangwenshuang from Getty Images via Canva Corteva (CTVA) shares soared 11% today after JPMorgan argued that the part of the company left behind by last week’s spin-off is the bargain. Corteva finished spinning off its seed and genetics business, now Vylor, on Thursday. That day, Corteva’s own stock reset almost 85% lower, since most of its value had gone with the seeds. What’s left is a crop chemicals company worth about $9 billion. Before today’s open, JPMorgan analyst Jeffrey Zekauskas raised Corteva to Overweight from Neutral, with a $19 price target. Here’s his pitch in one line: “Corteva is the cast off: and we think it is undervalued at the current price.” JPMorgan thinks a “high-quality” crop chemical company is worth about $21 a share, before environmental liabilities. Even after today’s jump, the $19 target means [nearly 40%] upside. Shares were up about 3% before the open. By mid-morning Barron’s had joined in with a piece headlined “Corteva Stock Can Gain 50% After Post-Spin Confusion,” and the stock kept climbing. Spin-offs often leave one side orphaned. Plenty of investors likely owned Corteva for its seeds. Some of last week’s selling probably came from them. JPMorgan isn’t alone, either. On Monday, Oppenheimer cut its Corteva target to $17 from $95 to reflect the split, and it kept its Outperform rating. The main risk is the thing JPMorgan’s $21 valuation leaves out: environmental liabilities. It is the biggest unknown in the stock. Corteva reports its third quarter on Wednesday, Nov. 11, after the close. It will be the company’s first report since the split. Last week the market priced Corteva like an afterthought, and two analysts now have targets well above where it trades. Of course, Corteva has been a standalone crop chemicals company for less than a week, so November’s numbers will be the first real test. title: Solana Releases Open-Source DvP Settlement Standard Shaped by J.P. Morgan - Startup Fortune
content: J.P. Morgan already settled a $50 million Galaxy Digital bond on Solana in December using this exact method, paid out entirely in Circle's USDC stablecoin instead of traditional clearing rails. J.P. Morgan helped shape it. A top-five U.S. bank spent months teaching a public blockchain its own playbook for how institutional trades should settle, closing the days-long gap where a deal can still collapse after both sides agree. The Solana Foundation on October 6 released Solana DvP, an open-source escrow program that gives banks and asset managers a standardized way to settle tokenized trades atomically on-chain, built with input from J.P. Morgan, according to CoinDesk and Decrypt. The program is released under an MIT license, and it compresses what is normally a multi-day clearinghouse process, where a security moves one way and cash moves the other on separate rails, into a single transaction. Either both legs settle together, or neither does. That single fact is the whole point. Delivery-versus-payment, or DvP, exists because settlement risk is real money: if you deliver a bond and the buyer's payment never lands, or you get paid and the seller never delivers, someone eats the loss. Traditional securities markets manage that risk with clearinghouses, custodians and a settlement cycle that typically runs two business days. Solana's version collapses that into one atomic transaction with finality in seconds. J.P. Morgan didn't write code for this. According to CoinDesk's reporting, the bank fed the project with its own settlement experience, shaping requirements around deadlines, escrow isolation, and the token features regulated issuers actually need, including pausable tokens and transfer hooks under Solana's Token-2022 standard. That's a bank telling a public blockchain foundation what compliance officers will actually sign off on, not a bank running its own private ledger and calling it innovation. The bank already has a live transaction to point to. In December 2025, J.P. Morgan arranged a $50 million U.S. commercial paper issuance for Galaxy Digital directly on Solana, according to Davis Polk, which advised on the deal. J.P. Morgan created the on-chain commercial paper token and handled the DvP settlement itself, with both the issuance and redemption proceeds paid in Circle's USDC. Coinbase and Franklin Templeton bought the paper, and Coinbase provided private-key custody. It was one of the first debt issuances of its kind on a U.S. public blockchain. Citi and Coinbase expanded their year-old partnership on September 28, wiring Coinbase's stablecoin conversion and settlement rails directly into Citi's corporate payments infrastructure. Businesses using Citi's Virtual Account Wallet and Spring platform can now send and accept stablecoin payments without ever holding the tokens themselves. - Citi using Coinbase for corporate stablecoin payments - how banks integrate cryptocurrency into payment processing That deal was a one-off, built and settled by J.P. Morgan's own team. Solana DvP is the attempt to turn that one-off into infrastructure anyone can use. Nick Ducoff, the Solana Foundation's head of institutional growth, has pointed to deals like the Galaxy Digital paper as evidence of real demand from institutions for high-speed public blockchains, not just pilots that never issue a second trade. Under the hood, Solana DvP leans entirely on Token-2022 extensions and standard USDC, with no custom program required to hold assets in escrow during settlement. Bonds or other instruments are created in a default frozen state, unlockable only for whitelisted, compliant counterparties. A settlement agent coordinates the trade without ever taking custody of either side's assets, which is the detail that actually matters to a bank's legal team: nobody but the two counterparties ends up holding the other side's money or securities mid-trade. Here's the real competitive angle. Ethereum has run tokenization pilots for years, and J.P. Morgan's own Kinexys platform has settled tokenized Treasuries against bank deposits using Chainlink's cross-chain protocol as far back as May 2025. What Solana is now offering is different: a standard built with a major bank's input but released openly, for any institution to adopt without needing J.P. Morgan to arrange the deal. If asset managers and other banks pick it up, Solana gets to claim the settlement layer for real-world asset tokenization before Ethereum's more fragmented tooling catches up. If they don't, it's another well-designed piece of infrastructure sitting mostly unused. Frankly, the test now isn't whether the code works. It's whether a second bank, one that didn't help write the spec, actually runs a trade through it. title: Solana Debuts Institutional Settlement Standard With J.P. Morgan Input - Decrypt News
content:
Solana Debuts Institutional Settlement Standard With J.P. Morgan Input The Solana Foundation is making a direct play for institutional finance, launching an open-source program designed to let banks settle trades on the network with the certainty they expect from traditional markets. Announced Monday, the tool, called Solana DvP, is an open-source escrow program that gives financial institutions a standardized API for delivery-versus-payment settlement, the bedrock mechanism that ensures an asset and its payment change hands simultaneously. Released under the permissive MIT license, it aims to bring that settlement guarantee to public blockchain infrastructure as a reusable standard rather than the bespoke smart contracts institutional trades have typically relied on. The foundation said J.P. Morgan provided input on institutional settlement practices that shaped the design. "Atomic settlement removes counterparty risk that is inherent in traditional finance," said Catherine Gu, the foundation's head of product for digital assets, adding that the program offers institutions a single open standard "with finality in seconds instead of days." Rhodel D'souza, J.P. Morgan's head of markets digital assets, said a shared, open standard for atomic delivery-versus-payment is "exactly the kind of foundational infrastructure institutional market participants require." In conventional markets, delivery-versus-payment runs through a multi-day chain of clearinghouses, depositories and custodians that can tie up capital for a day or two. Solana DvP compresses that into a single atomic transaction, where both legs settle together or neither does. The program supports SPL Token and Token-2022, including extensions regulated issuers depend on like permanent delegate, pausable tokens and transfer hooks, and has undergone external security audits. The foundation said it plans to add privacy features so settlements can be kept confidential. The launch builds on Solana's growing pull among institutions chasing tokenized real-world assets. title: Cambridge and London Life Sciences Showcase returns during JPM Healthcare Week 2027 - News-Medical
content:
o2h co-discovery has announced that the Cambridge × London Life Sciences Showcase will return for its second edition during J.P. Morgan Healthcare Week 2027 in San Francisco. The event brings together two of the UK's leading life sciences ecosystems, Cambridge and London, providing emerging companies with an international platform to present their science, innovation and growth opportunities directly to investors, pharma leaders and strategic partners. The showcase is organized and supported by Cancer Research Horizons, o2h co-discovery, Mishcon de Reya, Wellcome Genome Campus and Cambridge University Health Partners, with additional supporting partners expected to join. With capacity for 250 delegates, the 2027 event will build on the inaugural showcase, with a focused program centerd on company discovery, investor engagement and meaningful ecosystem connections. This year, companies are invited to apply for one of 20 available pitch slots. Companies will be selected based on scientific innovation, potential impact on human health, stage of development, commercial potential, investment readiness, and links to the Cambridge and London life sciences ecosystems. Each submission will be independently reviewed by a selection panel comprising showcase partners and leading voices from the ecosystem. The program will bring together a broad mix of investors, including venture capital, private equity, family offices and sovereign wealth investors, and will introduce a Reverse Pitch VC format, giving founders and attendees direct insight into investor priorities and investment criteria. Cambridge and London bring together world-leading universities, hospitals, investors, technology companies and an increasingly important AI and life sciences ecosystem. We want to bring the people, companies and ideas together with the wider life sciences community at one of the world’s major healthcare gatherings. We are grateful to our supporters and sponsors for helping us bring the Cambridge and London ecosystems to the global stage once again, and for being part of this growing platform for collaboration and connection.” Patrick Farrant, Partner, Mishcon de Reya, said: “Life sciences is a key focus for Mishcon, and we are looking forward to heading back to San Francisco for JPM Healthcare Week 2027. After a fantastic Cambridge x London Life Sciences Showcase last year, we're delighted to be supporting the event again. The connection between the Cambridge and US life sciences ecosystems has never been more important, with growing investment, partnerships and transatlantic collaboration helping innovative companies scale and bring new technologies to market. We're looking forward to some great discussions, fresh perspectives and catching up with friends and contacts from across the ecosystem.” Opportunities remain available for organizations interested in sponsoring or supporting the Showcase to become part of an initiative connecting the Cambridge and London life sciences ecosystems with the global investment and industry community during J.P. Morgan Healthcare Week. title: People on the Move: World Bank, HSBC, J.P. Morgan, IA Global - Global Finance Magazine
content: Global news and insight for corporate finance professionals Global news and insight for corporate finance professionals Home  Banking  People on the Move: World Bank, HSBC, J.P. Morgan, IA Global Major executive moves and leadership changes across the finance industry. This article appears in the September 2026 issue of Global Finance Magazine. The World Bank Group appointed Michael Kremer to be the organization’s chief economist and senior vice president for development economics. Most recently, he served as director of the University of Chicago’s Development Innovation Lab, where he researched economic growth, technological change, and development economics. Kermer, Abhijit Banerjee, and Esther Duflo jointly won the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2019 for their “experimental approach to alleviating global poverty. Kremer “has spent his career not just identifying what works in development but proving it at scale,” said Ajay Banga, President of the World Bank Group. “That is exactly the kind of thinking we need.”           —Rob Daly After more than a decade at HSBC, Pam Kaur will step down as Group CFO, a position she has held since January 2025, before the bank’s 2027 annual meeting. She will assume an advisory role to support Group CEO Georges Elherdy and ensure a smooth transition for her successor. Kaur began her career in 2013 as group head of internal audit before advancing to the head of wholesale market and credit risk, group chief risk officer, group chief risk and compliance officer, and eventually group CFO. Brendan Nelson, HSBC Group Holding plc chairman, praised Kaur for her “strong judgment and integrity.” She will leave the Group CFO role with the firm’s “deepest thanks and best wishes,” he added. —Rob Daly J.P. Morgan named Nelle Miller and William Sinclair as co-CEOs of its U.S. Private Bank in September. The pair leads the firm’s $2.4 trillion U.S. private banking business, overseeing more than 5,500 professionals across 57 offices who serve the wealthiest individuals, family offices, and institutions nationwide. The appointments follow the July 2025 naming of David Frame as global CEO of J.P. Morgan Private Bank. Miller and Sinclair joined in 2002 and 2007, respectively. Miller currently heads the firm’s New York market, while Sinclair leads the Financial Leaders Group. “We have a fantastic franchise, with exceptional people and an unparalleled breadth of capabilities,” Sinclair said.      —Anthony Noto IA Global Capital, a technology-focused investment bank with offices in New York and London, announced that Jules Wurlod has joined the firm as managing director. Wurlod has served as M&A director for circular businesses at Houlihan Lokey since 2020, focusing on circular technology services such as device-as-a-service, IT asset management, IT asset disposition, recommerce, and trade-in. He previously worked as a project leader at Boston Consulting Group, advising Fortune 500 companies and government officials across Europe and the Middle East on corporate strategy and sustainability. —Anthony Noto
